newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Three senior central bank executives and two police generals are suspended from duty and face investigation over the collapse of a Bangkok Bank of Commerce case. The suspensions, ordered by the prime minister, follow a 20-day row over who was responsible for a legal blunder that raised questions about coordination among law enforcement agencies and banking regulators. (BANGKOK POST, BUSINESS DAY)

- Charoen Pokphand Group (CP) chairman Dhanin Chearavanont has denied that Thailand's largest agro conglomerate made financial contributions to U.S. President Bill Clinton's 1996 election campaign, as U.S. probes of campaign financing scandals focused on Asian companies. Dhanin says last June's "coffee meeting" with Clinton at the White House was simply an exchange of views about Thailand. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The likelihood that the new constitution will be approved this year has increased with the opposition Democrat Party and the government's key legal expert voicing support for the three main chapters which will comprise the new charter. The Constitution Drafting Assembly earlier approved a chapter concerning "people's rights and their participation in politics" and a chapter on "monitoring the use of state power". (THE NATION)

- The state of the economy, fiscal policies, problems in the property sector and monetary policies were all discussed at a meeting yesterday between Finance Ministry officials, led by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, and analysts from Moody's Investors Service. The talks touched on measures taken by the Government earlier this week to assist finance companies facing liquidity shortage. Amnuay explained that the measures were meant to benefit all affected parties: depositors, creditors and investors. (BUSINESS DAY, THE NATION)

- The Association of Finance Companies, on behalf of the ailing finance firms obliged to raise capital immediately, has pledged to urgently seek discussions with the Bank of Thailand on the rationale of the measure. The measure, as well as another which requires all bank and finance firms to set aside further provisions, will also be included on the agenda of the association's annual meeting scheduled to be held in Pattaya over the weekend. (THE NATION)
